concepts.title: Science as a Process of Inquiry
concepts.definition: Science is a continuous process of asking questions, observing carefully, and seeking evidence to understand the natural world.
concepts.key_idea: Science is not just a collection of facts; it is an ongoing process of inquiry driven by curiosity.
question_patterns: What is science as a process of inquiry?
How is science more than just a collection of facts?
Why is asking questions important in science?
Give one example of scientific inquiry in daily life.
How does curiosity drive the process of science?

solution_steps.explain: Recognise a natural phenomenon or event that needs explanation.
Make careful observations and gather information to answer the question.
Use the evidence to form an explanation that can be tested and improved.

worked_examples.question: What is science as a process of inquiry?
worked_examples.solution: Science is a continuous process of asking questions, observing, and seeking evidence to understand the world.
worked_examples.answer: Science is a continuous process of asking questions, observing, and seeking evidence.

worked_examples.question: How is science more than just a collection of facts?
worked_examples.solution: Science is a way of finding answers through inquiry, not merely a list of facts to memorise.
worked_examples.answer: Science is a way of finding answers through inquiry, not just a list of facts.

worked_examples.question: Give one example of scientific inquiry in daily life.
worked_examples.solution: Asking why food spoils and then observing that it spoils faster in warm, damp conditions is an example of inquiry.
worked_examples.answer: Asking why food spoils and observing that it spoils faster when warm and damp.

exercises.question: Why is asking questions important in science?
Give one example of curiosity leading to a scientific question.
How does evidence help in the process of inquiry?

concepts.title: Evolution of Scientific Knowledge
concepts.definition: Scientific knowledge grows and changes over time as new observations, tools, and experiments improve our understanding.
concepts.key_idea: Scientific ideas are not fixed; they evolve as new evidence is discovered.
question_patterns: How does scientific knowledge change over time?
Why is scientific knowledge not fixed?
Give one example of a scientific idea that changed.
How do new tools help science evolve?
Why do scientists revise their theories?

solution_steps.explain: Note the earlier understanding or theory about a phenomenon.
Look for new observations or experiments that challenge the old idea.
Describe how the new evidence led to a revised or new understanding.

worked_examples.question: How does scientific knowledge change over time?
worked_examples.solution: As new observations and tools appear, scientists revise their ideas to match the new evidence.
worked_examples.answer: New observations and tools lead scientists to revise their ideas.

worked_examples.question: Give one example of a scientific idea that changed.
worked_examples.solution: People once thought the Earth was flat, but explorations and evidence showed it is round.
worked_examples.answer: The idea that the Earth is flat changed to the Earth being round.

worked_examples.question: How do new tools help science evolve?
worked_examples.solution: The microscope let scientists see cells, which led to the cell theory and a new understanding of life.
worked_examples.answer: The microscope revealed cells, leading to the cell theory.

exercises.question: Why is scientific knowledge not fixed?
Give one example of a theory that was revised.
How does new evidence affect old ideas?

concepts.title: Science and Experiments
concepts.definition: The scientific method is a structured process of observation, hypothesis, experiment, analysis, and conclusion used to answer questions reliably.
concepts.key_idea: The scientific method turns curiosity into reliable answers through a step-by-step process.
question_patterns: What are the steps of the scientific method?
What is a hypothesis?
How does an experiment test a hypothesis?
Why is a conclusion important in the scientific method?
Give one example of using the scientific method.

solution_steps.explain: Notice something interesting and form a clear question about it.
Make a testable guess called a hypothesis and test it with a fair experiment.
Study the results and decide whether they support the hypothesis or not.

worked_examples.question: List the main steps of the scientific method in order.
worked_examples.solution: The steps are observation, hypothesis, experiment, analysis, and conclusion.
worked_examples.answer: Observation, hypothesis, experiment, analysis, conclusion.

worked_examples.question: A student sees ice melting faster on a metal plate than on a plastic one. State a hypothesis they could test.
worked_examples.solution: A possible hypothesis is: metal transfers heat faster than plastic, so ice melts quicker on metal.
worked_examples.answer: Metal transfers heat faster than plastic, melting ice quicker.

worked_examples.question: Why is a conclusion needed after an experiment?
worked_examples.solution: A conclusion tells us whether the results support the hypothesis, so we know what we learned.
worked_examples.answer: A conclusion tells us whether the hypothesis is supported by the results.

exercises.question: What is a hypothesis?
Why must an experiment be fair?
Write the steps of the scientific method in order.

concepts.title: Role of Observation and Experimentation
concepts.definition: Observation is carefully noting what happens, and experimentation is testing ideas under controlled conditions to gather reliable evidence.
concepts.key_idea: Careful observation and fair experiments are the foundations of trustworthy scientific knowledge.
question_patterns: Why is observation important in science?
What is the role of experimentation in science?
How does a fair experiment help?
Give one example of observation leading to a discovery.
Why must experiments be repeated?

solution_steps.explain: Use senses and tools to note what happens in detail.
Change only one variable at a time and keep other conditions the same.
Write down the results and repeat the experiment to check reliability.

worked_examples.question: Why is observation important in science?
worked_examples.solution: Observation provides the facts and patterns that scientists use to build explanations.
worked_examples.answer: Observation provides the facts and patterns for explanations.

worked_examples.question: Give one example of observation leading to a discovery.
worked_examples.solution: Alexander Fleming observed mould killing bacteria, which led to the discovery of penicillin.
worked_examples.answer: Fleming observed mould killing bacteria, leading to penicillin.

worked_examples.question: Why must experiments be repeated?
worked_examples.solution: Repeating an experiment checks that the results are reliable and not due to chance.
worked_examples.answer: Repeating checks that results are reliable and not due to chance.

exercises.question: What is the role of experimentation in science?
How does a fair experiment help?
Give one example of careful observation in daily life.

concepts.title: Science and Society
concepts.definition: Science influences society by improving health, agriculture, transport, and communication, while society guides the problems science chooses to solve.
concepts.key_idea: Science and society shape each other; scientific progress improves lives and society sets new questions.
question_patterns: How does science affect society?
Give one example of science improving health.
How does society influence science?
Why is science important for agriculture?
Name one way science improves communication.

solution_steps.explain: Find a problem in society such as disease, food shortage, or poor transport.
Determine which scientific idea or invention addresses that need.
Describe how the solution improves people's lives.

worked_examples.question: How does science affect society?
worked_examples.solution: Science improves health, food, transport, and communication, making life safer and easier.
worked_examples.answer: Science improves health, food, transport, and communication.

worked_examples.question: Give one example of science improving health.
worked_examples.solution: Vaccines, developed through science, prevent diseases and save millions of lives.
worked_examples.answer: Vaccines prevent diseases and save lives.

worked_examples.question: How does society influence science?
worked_examples.solution: Society's needs, such as clean energy, guide scientists to study and solve those problems.
worked_examples.answer: Society's needs guide the problems scientists choose to solve.

exercises.question: Why is science important for agriculture?
Name one way science improves communication.
Give one example of a social need guiding science.

concepts.title: Famous Scientists and Their Contributions
concepts.definition: Scientists such as Newton, Darwin, Curie, and Kalam made important discoveries that advanced our understanding of nature and improved technology.
concepts.key_idea: Individual scientists have made key contributions that shaped modern science.
question_patterns: Name one famous scientist and their contribution.
What did Marie Curie discover?
How did Newton contribute to science?
What was A.P.J. Abdul Kalam known for?
Give one example of a scientist whose work changed the world.

solution_steps.explain: Note the name of the scientist and their field of work.
Describe the discovery or invention they are known for.
Show how their work changed science or society.

worked_examples.question: What did Marie Curie discover?
worked_examples.solution: Marie Curie discovered the elements radium and polonium and studied radioactivity.
worked_examples.answer: Radium, polonium, and radioactivity.

worked_examples.question: How did Newton contribute to science?
worked_examples.solution: Newton discovered the laws of motion and gravitation, explaining how objects move.
worked_examples.answer: Laws of motion and gravitation.

worked_examples.question: What was A.P.J. Abdul Kalam known for?
worked_examples.solution: A.P.J. Abdul Kalam was known for his work on India's space and missile programmes and inspiring young scientists.
worked_examples.answer: India's space and missile programmes and inspiring youth.

exercises.question: Name one famous scientist and their contribution.
What did Charles Darwin contribute to science?
Give one example of a scientist whose work changed the world.

concepts.title: Branches of Science
concepts.definition: Science is divided into branches such as physics, chemistry, biology, and earth science, each studying a different part of nature.
concepts.key_idea: Different branches of science study different aspects of the natural world.
question_patterns: Name three branches of science.
What does biology study?
What does physics study?
Which branch of science studies living things?
Give one example of a question chemistry tries to answer.

solution_steps.explain: Decide what the question is about, such as living things, forces, or chemicals.
Find which branch of science studies that topic.
Give an example that shows what that branch studies.

worked_examples.question: Name three branches of science.
worked_examples.solution: Three branches are physics, chemistry, and biology.
worked_examples.answer: Physics, chemistry, biology.

worked_examples.question: Which branch of science studies living things?
worked_examples.solution: Biology studies living things such as plants and animals.
worked_examples.answer: Biology.

worked_examples.question: What does physics study?
worked_examples.solution: Physics studies forces, energy, light, and motion.
worked_examples.answer: Forces, energy, light, and motion.

exercises.question: What does chemistry study?
Name one branch of science and what it studies.
Which branch studies the Earth and its rocks?
